---
description: What a compaction's summary keeps and drops. This is the text a summary of a session's earlier turns is written from, and the one home of what it keeps. What the Author did in the turns being summarized follows it, laid out by the carried part, after the summary so far where there is one; when those turns are more than the model takes they are sent in pieces, oldest first, each after the summary written from the pieces before it. The notice the Author gets beforehand is a rule of its own, save-before-compaction.
---
Write what the Author must still have after the detail is gone, and nothing else:

1. Rulings made, and why, so that the same question gets the same answer.
2. What was allowed to be invented, and within what bounds.
3. What is intended and not yet shown: setups, reveals, where the scene is going.
4. What was looked up, and where it was, so that it need not be looked up again.
5. Anything the player asked for that still stands.

Leave out what the chat history and the story record already tell: what happened, and who said what.

Where a summary so far comes first, yours takes its place: keep from it what still stands.
